clue.text: Taking meal when touring a flat — useful start?

indicators.note: to tour something is to go round it, so the meal word wraps round the letter A

parts.note: taking a midday meal is lunching
a pad is slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: Someone moving into a flat suggests a meal out as a handy beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link; 'touring' puts LUNCHING round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket's launch platform is literally the place where a start is made, hence a figurative springboard.

clue.text: Bird having a plaintive warble initially in heather

indicators.note: the letters are placed inside the word for heather

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather

indicators.note: signals taking the opening letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird sings its mournful song from a patch of moorland heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes P and W from 'plaintive warble'; with A they go inside LING.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing, or peewit, is a crested plover of farmland and moor.

clue.text: Winning part of cycling race is put in the shade

parts.note: being up means ahead or winning in a contest
races such as the Tour de France are run in stages

explanation.surface: A rider's victory on one leg of a bike race is overshadowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine someone and draw attention away from them is to put them in the shade.

clue.text: Group of pupils on walk to find powerful animal

definitions.meaning: a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs is called by this reptile's name in Britain
a large toothed reptile of rivers, strong and dangerous

explanation.surface: A school party out walking comes across a mighty beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a British school line walking two by two, and the big reptile.

clue.text: At home leaders of company under review suffer

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: signals the first letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Bosses of a firm under scrutiny have a hard time at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under review' looks like a reversal signal, but those words just supply their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it on yourself and suffer it.

clue.text: One overly full of cheer?

parts.note: cheer can mean food and drink, so someone stuffed with it is a greedy eater, not a jolly person

explanation.surface: Someone who seems too cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheer' here is the old sense of food and drink, as in 'good cheer' at a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who eats to excess ends up overly full of food and drink.

clue.text: American tenor featuring in song in country

indicators.note: appearing within something, so these letters go inside the song

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song
US is short for United States, hence American
T is the abbreviation for tenor in vocal scoring

explanation.surface: An American tenor sings a song set in some country.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a central European nation with Vienna as its capital.

clue.text: I'm getting over second season on river bringing bad luck

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upward, so these two letters are read backwards

parts.note: Advent is the church season before Christmas
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone recovering from a stretch spent by a river finds things going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'getting over' turns the word upward; 'on' just links, since each piece sits below the one before.
explanation.definitionFit: A misadventure is an accident or piece of misfortune.

clue.text: Endless time OAP's spent in type of painting

indicators.note: used up or worn out, signalling the letters are rearranged
without its end, so the last letter of the word time is dropped

parts.note: OAP is an old-age pensioner; with the 's the letters O, A, P, S are used

explanation.surface: A pensioner whiles away hours on an art style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts TIME to TIM; 'spent' rearranges TIM plus OAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the technique of laying on paint thickly so brushstrokes stand out.

clue.text: Advice from local authority reportedly

indicators.note: signals a word that sounds like the one suggested

parts.note: a council is a local government body

explanation.surface: Guidance said to come from the town hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is a formal word for advice or guidance given.

clue.text: They reveal specialists in invention?

parts.note: invention can mean making things up, i.e. lying; machines that expose fibbers spot experts in it

explanation.surface: Something that exposes clever inventors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invention' suggests patents and engineers, but here it means fabricating stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Polygraph machines claim to detect people who are fibbing, i.e. those skilled in making things up.

clue.text: Modelled a toga — it is done in a ruffled style

indicators.note: shaped or remodelled, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a toga, worn in a dishevelled way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' just links; 'Modelled' rearranges A TOGA IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is a musical direction meaning to play in an agitated, restless manner.

clue.text: Religious class on island for one having finished work

parts.note: RE is Religious Education, a school subject
Tiree is an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A scripture lesson on a remote island for a pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just links the two pieces, the first placed before the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has stopped working for good, typically through age, has retired from employment.

clue.text: Victor fit? It's far from clear

parts.note: Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ague is a feverish fit of shivering

explanation.surface: Is Victor in good shape? Nobody really knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like an adjective meaning healthy; it is a noun, a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vague is unclear, hazy or imprecise.

clue.text: Hint is in a tune that's off-key

indicators.note: out of tune, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A clue lies in a melody that is out of pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to suggest something indirectly, to imply rather than state.

clue.text: Gloomy figure after part of weekend with university rector, in short

indicators.note: the number comes after the other pieces

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday
R is an abbreviation for rector
nine is a number, or figure

explanation.surface: A miserable number follows a Saturday with a college head.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine describes a dark, sullen temperament, once linked to the planet Saturn.

clue.text: One selling in the rag trade?

definitions.text: One selling in the rag trade?

parts.words: One selling in the rag trade?
parts.note: the rag trade means clothing, but a rag is also slang for a newspaper, so this is a seller of papers

explanation.surface: A clothes salesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rag trade' is the clothing business; here a rag is a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopkeeper who sells newspapers and magazines trades in rags in the slang sense.

clue.text: Aspiring blue down, having left North, for training

indicators.note: training means putting through exercises, signalling a rearrangement
the named letter has departed from the word

explanation.surface: A sad sportsman, his northern days behind him, goes into training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' takes N out of DOWN; 'for training' rearranges BLUE DOW. A Blue is also an Oxbridge sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A would-be performer is an aspiring one, hoping to become something.

clue.text: Place in office getting a purpose, we're told

indicators.note: signals a word that sounds like the phrase given

parts.note: a point is a purpose, as in 'what's the point?'

explanation.surface: Someone gets a job and a reason for being, we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to install them in a post or position.

clue.text: Elevated position in game but bowled out first

indicators.note: the letter is taken out from the front of the word

parts.note: bridge is a card game
B is the cricket scoring abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: In a cricket match, being bowled out early puts a player in a high spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long raised strip of land, a high vantage point.

clue.text: Selfish type in an estate?

parts.note: an estate is also an estate car, so this is an inconsiderate driver

explanation.surface: A self-centred neighbour on a housing development.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is a British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggressive or inconsiderate motorist who hogs the carriageway is given this nickname.

clue.text: Abandon rental property in tiny amount of rain

parts.note: to drop a plan is to abandon it
a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: Giving up a rented flat because of a little rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A single small drop of liquid, such as a raindrop, is a droplet.

clue.text: Criminal seizing power in America and Peru possibly? Right

parts.note: US stands for United States, i.e. America

indicators.note: signals one possible rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A villain grabs control in the Americas, perhaps in Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurper wrongfully takes a throne or authority, an illegal grab for control.

clue.text: Jolly character's word of acknowledgement

definitions.meaning: the Jolly ... is the pirate flag, so this name completes the phrase
radio operators say this to mean message received

explanation.surface: A cheerful fellow says 'got it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename completes the pirate flag's name and is also radio-speak for message understood.

clue.text: Fuss among two notes in computer data

indicators.note: the word for fuss sits between the two notes

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
ut is the old name for the sol-fa note now called do
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A commotion between two musical notes in a computer file.
explanation.walkthrough: UT is the original name of the first sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: A display or printout of information from a computer or instrument is called by this name.

clue.text: Leading journalist on way out in a turbulent state?

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the senior journalist
to be on the way out is to be dying

explanation.surface: A top newspaper editor nearing the end, in turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that swirls in circular currents is churning, hence turbulent.

clue.text: Medical device in hospital curtailed alarm

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: an alert is a warning or alarm

explanation.surface: A device on a ward cut off before the alarm finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An asthmatic uses a handheld device to breathe medicine into the lungs.

clue.text: White gel twerp spilt after removing onset of pain for boxer

indicators.note: spilt suggests things knocked over and scattered, signalling a rearrangement
the named letter is taken away first
signals the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A fool knocks over a pot of white gel and hurts himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onset of pain' gives P, which 'after removing' takes out; 'spilt' then rearranges the remaining twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer fighting in the weight class between lightweight and middleweight is named by it.
